headline: Dubai Finale: Hatton fires 66 to win by 5 at -15; McIlroy seals 8th Race to Dubai
whyCareReason: Tyrrell Hatton cards a closing 66 to win by 5 shots at 15 under par (273), while Rory McIlroy birdies the 16th to finish solo 2nd (-10, 278) and seal his 8th Race to Dubai title by 125 points over Eugenio Chacarra.
teaser: Tyrrell Hatton cards a closing 66 to finish 15 under (273) and win the DP World Tour Championship by 5 strokes. Rory McIlroy (67, 278, -10) holds off Eugenio Chacarra by 125 points to capture his eighth Race to Dubai title, equalling Colin Montgomerie.
story: Tyrrell Hatton closed in ruthless fashion to claim his ninth DP World Tour title and sixth Rolex Series victory on Sunday, 15 November, firing a bogey-free six-under 66 to win the DP World Tour Championship by five shots at 15-under-par 273 at the Earth Course, Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai. The season-long Race to Dubai delivered drama down to the 72nd green: Spain's Eugenio Chacarra carded a 68 to share third place at nine-under 279, but Rory McIlroy produced a clinical five-under 67, highlighted by a clutch birdie on the par-4 16th, to finish solo second at 10-under 278. That runner-up finish sealed McIlroy's eighth European Tour Order of Merit and fifth consecutive Harry Vardon Trophy by just 125 points, matching Colin Montgomerie's legendary benchmark.
stakes: Hatton wins his ninth DP World Tour title while McIlroy clinches his record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai crown by 125 points over Chacarra.
rivalryAngle: McIlroy edges Chacarra by 125 points across the entire European Tour season after birdieing the 16th hole on Sunday afternoon in Dubai.
funFacts: Tyrrell Hatton leads on 207 (-9, 70-69-68) with Victor Perez one back on 208 (-8, 69-72-67).
Eugenio Chacarra shot 68 to tie Rory McIlroy (72) at five-under 211 in fourth place.
Sunday 15 November is the fourth and final round of the $10 million season finale in Dubai.
